metadata.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP?

data.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP?
data.summary:
At the **2021 São Paulo Grand Prix (Brazilian GP)** on **November 14, 2021**, a major controversy occurred between championship rivals Max Verstappen (Red Bull) and Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) [1.4]:

### The Incident (Lap 48)
On **Lap 48**, Hamilton used DRS to attempt an overtake around the outside of Verstappen into the Turn 4 left-hander (*Descida do Lago*) [1.2, 1.3]. To defend, Verstappen braked extremely late on the inside line [1.3]. Consequently, Verstappen's car drifted wide on the corner exit, forcing both drivers to run completely off the track onto the asphalt run-off area [1.2, 1.3, 1.5]. Verstappen maintained his lead [1.2]. 

### Immediate Stewarding Decision
The FIA race stewards noted the incident but opted not to investigate [1.2]. Learning of the decision on the team radio, Hamilton sarcastically replied: *"Of course, man, of course."* [1.2] 

### Right of Review and Regulation Conflict
On **November 16, 2021**, Mercedes petitioned for a **Right of Review under Article 14.1.1 of the FIA International Sporting Code (ISC)** [1.10]. They presented "new and significant" evidence: the forward-facing onboard camera footage from Verstappen's car, which had not been available to the stewards or the live broadcast during the race (only Verstappen's rear-facing feed was active) [1.7, 1.10]. 

Mercedes argued that Verstappen violated rules regarding **"forcing another driver off the track"** (Chapter IV, Appendix L of the ISC) [1.8, 1.9]. However, on **November 19, 2021**, the stewards denied Mercedes’ petition, ruling that while the footage was indeed new, it was not "significant" enough to overturn their original decision of no further action [1.10].

### Race Outcome
Despite the incident, Hamilton regrouped, caught Verstappen, and successfully completed a DRS-assisted overtake for the lead at Turn 4 on **Lap 59**, going on to win the race [1.2].
